title: Census Bureau Data API (ACS, decennial census, population estimates)
questions: median household income by county in a state
median home value and rent in a county
share of adults with a bachelor's degree by state

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser after replacing {API_KEY} with your own free Census key (https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html), or run download_data.sh / download_data.ps1 (one command; asks for the key with hidden input); save each JSON file under the name shown and upload it, then --ingest. Without the bundle: on https://data.census.gov search the table (e.g. B19013), choose the geography and year, and use Download Table (CSV); upload it and say it is a data.census.gov export (its layout differs: one estimate and one margin-of-error column per geography).

cache.why: Only API metadata is cached on disk (variables.json lists for --search and the dataset discovery checks behind 'latest'); it changes once a release. Data queries are never cached: data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: Census Bureau statistics are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); the Census Data API Terms of Service require the notice that the product uses the API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau.

notices: This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau.
citation: U.S. Census Bureau, {dataset}, Census Data API (api.census.gov), retrieved {retrieved_long}.

audit_hooks.why: ACS figures are survey estimates; a report must give or discuss their margins of error (90% level) before comparing places or years.

clarify: ACS 1-year (latest single year, only areas of 65,000+ people) or 5-year (all areas, pooled over five years, less current)? Do not compare a 1-year with a 5-year estimate.
Report estimates alone or with margins of error (90%), and test differences for significance? Small areas often have large margins.
Which geography vintage? County and place boundaries and codes change (Connecticut planning regions replaced counties from ACS 2022); 5-year estimates use the boundaries of their final year.
